articles.title: Jensen Huang's return revives an old Wall Street trade: Bet on the comeback CEO
articles.summary: Investors have often cheered when big-name CEOs like Jensen Huang return.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang's return as CEO of Nvidia ( NVDA ) could be good for more than a one-day pop in its stock price.

Just look at the evidence from the case studies on the returns of founders like Apple's ( AAPL ) Steve Jobs, Starbucks' ( SBUX ) founder Howard Schultz, and Charles Schwab's ( SCHW ) founder Charles Schwab.

A new analysis of six high-profile CEO returns by Rand Group Research found that four of the six companies outperformed the S&P 500 over the three years after their leaders returned.

The biggest winner was Apple, where Steve Jobs' return in September 1997 was followed by a staggering 414% stock gain, versus 59% for the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ). The stock price gain reflected Jobs' innovation streak, which led to world-changing products like the iPhone and iPod.

Charles Schwab shares climbed 141% after its founder returned in 2004 after a year to rejuvenate the brokerage house, according to a New York Times account .

Starbucks gained 78% under Howard Schultz when he returned in January 2008, compared with a 10% decline for the benchmark. Schultz moved quickly to improve operations from a then floundering business.

Google's Larry Page delivered an 84% gain after returning in 2011, also beating the market.

Disney ( DIS ) shares rose just 14% after Bob Iger returned in 2022, badly trailing the S&P 500's 67% gain, while Under Armour ( UA ) has fallen 40% since Kevin Plank returned in 2024.

The takeaway for Nvidia investors? A founder's return can be a powerful catalyst, particularly when that founder has a deep understanding of the business and a track record of creating shareholder value.

But it's no guarantee. Jensen Huang has the opportunity to join a pretty impressive comeback club — but he'll still have to deliver.

Shares of Nvidia fell nearly 4% in premarket trading on Tuesday after a 31.2% surge on news that founder Huang had been reinstated as CEO. That came just 12 days after he resigned amid a personal scandal and federal chip-export probes.

"Jensen will be on a mission," EMJ Capital founder Eric Jackson said on Sozzi Unleashed .

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show, the ' Power Players With Brian Sozzi' podcast and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

articles.title: Jensen Huang is back at Nvidia. Should AMD be worried?
articles.summary: AMD is in focus as it sees its biggest rival take a huge step to going back to business as usual.
articles.body:
When it comes to the AI trade, this has been the year of AMD ( AMD ). AMD's stock has sizzled, up 112% year to date compared to an 11.5% drop for its top rival Nvidia.

As Nvidia's ( NVDA ) founder Jensen Huang has been embroiled in scandal and the tech trade has been pressured, AMD shares have hung tough. The stock is down 12.2% over the past month versus a 22% decline for Nvidia.

The biggest question for AMD right now is this: Does Huang's stunning return as CEO of Nvidia mean bad news for AMD in 2027 and beyond?

Pros think AMD will be just fine, for now.

"I don't see how this changes it completely," Moor Insights & Strategy founder Patrick Moorhead said on Sozzi Unleashed . "I was saying early on when Jensen left that nothing changes for 18 months. And the reason is the supply chain is locked, the wafers are locked, data center configurations are locked around Nvidia design. So nothing would change, I think, if Jensen had been removed permanently."

Shares of Nvidia fell 5% in premarket trading on Tuesday after a 31.2% surge on news that founder Jensen Huang had been reinstated as CEO. That came just 12 days after he resigned amid a personal scandal and federal chip-export probes.

Interestingly, AMD shares rose 6.3% yesterday — a telling move that investors continue to believe in the AMD story.

CEO Lisa Su — Yahoo Finance's 2026 CEO of the Year award winner — surprised everyone by spending $8.2 billion to scoop up World Labs , gaining a true AI innovator that focuses on software for 3D environments.

World Labs was founded in 2024 and is led by Fei-Fei Li, a leading AI researcher known in tech circles as the "Godmother of AI." She was once the chief scientist at Google Cloud ( GOOG ).

Just a few weeks ago, AMD delivered a strong double beat in its third quarter earnings report. Third quarter sales jumped 45% year over year to a record $13.38 billion, comfortably surpassing Wall Street consensus estimates of roughly $13.06 billion.

Adjusted earnings climbed 74% to $2.09 per share, easily topping analyst projections of $1.94 per share.

The blowout performance was anchored by AMD's Data Center segment, where revenue surged 97% to a record $8.5 billion on robust demand for EPYC server processors and the production ramp of Instinct MI450 AI accelerators.

For the fourth quarter, AMD said it sees 50% sequential growth in data centers. In 2027, Su guided to revenue growing more than 80%, with server revenue doubling and data center AI more than doubling.

articles.title: Live updates: Huang return to Nvidia faces resistance; shutdown odds rising
articles.summary: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang was reinstated as the company’s CEO on Monday in a dramatic reversal by the chipmaker’s board following his resignation after the tech mogul admitted to affairs, which reportedly were with a woman suspected of having ties to Chinese intelligence and a subordinate. Huang returned to the company’s headquarters Monday to cheers…
articles.body:
Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang was reinstated as the company’s CEO on Monday in a dramatic reversal by the chipmaker’s board following his resignation after the tech mogul admitted to affairs, which reportedly were with a woman suspected of having ties to Chinese intelligence and a subordinate. Huang returned to the company’s headquarters Monday to cheers from employees . He vowed, in a video shared online, to “be a better CEO the second time around.” The decision to bring him back, which was praised by President Trump, drew scrutiny from lawmakers . The Commerce Department also moved Monday to place Megaspeed, a company at the center of the controversy over allegedly smuggling Nvidia chips to China, on its trade blacklist .

Additionally, Senate negotiators are racing the clock to find a deal to avoid a government shutdown before Christmas, but progress has been slowed by the leadership fight. The key roadblock? Defense funding and the Iran war.

Meanwhile, the Army’s planned detonation of explosive materials at an Iowa ammunition plant is set to proceed Wednesday, after Gov.-elect Rob Sand (D) deferred the decision to Trump and a federal appeals court declined to intervene .

A new group has also formed to urge Sen. Rand Paul (R-Ky.) to run for president in 2028. Read more in The Hill’s exclusive report .

The president will participate Tuesday in a Medal of Freedom ceremony, executive time and policy meetings. In the afternoon, he and first lady Melania Trump will host the annual Thanksgiving Turkey Pardon before heading to Florida for the holiday.

articles.title: India's first bullet train to begin trials on 50-km Surat-Bilimora stretch in May 2027 as electrification is completed and signalling work is expected to finish by January
articles.summary: Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor: India’s first bullet train project is likely to begin trial runs in May 2027, with preparations under way to test
articles.body: Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor: India’s first bullet train project is likely to begin trial runs in May 2027, with preparations under way to test the 50 kilometres long Surat-Bilimora stretch of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor first, Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said on Monday.The Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor, India’s first bullet train project, is being developed to establish high-speed rail connectivity between the two major cities.Speaking at a media briefing, Vaishnaw said electrification work on the section was complete, while signalling-related work was scheduled to be finished by January 2027.The overhead electrification system along the elevated stretch was energised on November 20, covering both tracks. The section uses a 2x25 kV traction system, and installation work at the Bilimora traction substation has also been completed.When will India get its first bullet train?Vaishnaw said the high-speed rail corridor would become operational in stages, rather than being opened along its entire length at one time.Under the proposed schedule, the Ahmedabad-Vapi section is expected to be completed by the end of 2027. The bullet train service is targeted to extend to Thane by 2029.The first round of trials will use the B-28 train, which has been built to run at speeds of up to 280 kmph.Vaishnaw explained that operating trains at speeds exceeding 240 kmph calls for specialised engineering, as the pressure forces generated while trains are in motion must be accounted for in the design of both the rolling stock and the supporting infrastructure.He said the B-28 train had cleared a squeeze test, during which it was subjected to pressure levels twice the atmospheric pressure expected during regular operations. The test was conducted to assess the train’s ability to withstand pressure-related stresses at high speeds.The minister also expressed satisfaction with the pace of construction in Maharashtra, including work on the undersea tunnel, describing the progress on these sections as encouraging.India makes bullet train for the first timeBEML Limited has secured a Rs 866.87 crore contract from Integral Coach Factory (ICF), Chennai, to manufacture two prototype bullet train, or high-speed train, sets designed to run at speeds exceeding 250 kmph. The trains will have a design speed of 280 kmph.The contract covers the design, manufacture and commissioning of two train sets, each comprising eight coaches.The trains will feature fully air-conditioned chair cars equipped with world-class passenger facilities, advanced onboard infotainment systems, reclining and rotatable seats, and dedicated amenities for divyangjans.To facilitate production, BEML has established a dedicated ‘Aditya’ High-Speed Rail Complex in Bengaluru for manufacturing the bullet trains.The trains, designated as B-28 train sets, will be built using advanced, precision-driven technologies. While bullet trains operating in countries such as Japan and across Europe are engineered to withstand cold climatic conditions, the Indian versions will be designed to cope with the country’s heat and dust.More bullet train projectsThe Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor is one of several ambitious rail infrastructure projects planned by Indian Railways. The Union Budget for this year announced seven additional high-speed rail corridors. Developing domestic capabilities to manufacture bullet trains could help India meet the rolling stock requirements of these proposed routes more cost-effectively.The seven proposed corridors are Mumbai-Pune, with a journey time of 48 minutes; Pune-Hyderabad, at 1 hour 55 minutes; Hyderabad-Bengaluru, at 2 hours; Hyderabad-Chennai, at 2 hours 55 minutes; Chennai-Bengaluru, at 1 hour 13 minutes; Delhi-Varanasi, at 3 hours 50 minutes; and Varanasi-Siliguri via Patna, at 2 hours 55 minutes.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: HPE stock declines as disappointing margin forecast outweighs upbeat guidance
articles.summary: HPE stock retreated following the server maker's quarterly results.
articles.body:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise ( HPE ) stock dropped 13% in premarket trading on Tuesday after the server and networking products maker reported fourth quarter results.

The company said it expects Cloud & AI operating margins to fall to about 14% in fiscal 2027, down from 18.4% in the latest quarter, raising concerns that pricing tailwinds are beginning to fade.

The outlook overshadowed better-than-expected 2027 revenue guidance and strong order growth. Quarterly cloud and AI revenue grew 68.6% from the same period a year earlier.

Shares of peer Dell ( DELL ) also fell 7% in premarket trading amid a broader retreat in the AI-related trade. Dell is scheduled to report earnings after Tuesday's market close.

HPE's board approved an additional $5 billion for share repurchases, bringing the company's total remaining authorization to about $7.3 billion. The company also declared a regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.17 per share.

HPE stock has surged by roughly 100% year to date.

articles.title: Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom lead chip stocks lower as AI trade comes under pressure
articles.summary: Chip giant Nvidia led semiconductor stocks lower on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Nvidia ( NVDA ) stock retreated 8% on Tuesday, giving back some of its 31% surge from the prior session after the board of the AI chip giant reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. Peers AMD ( AMD ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ) also declined from Monday's rebound as the overall AI trade came under renewed pressure.

Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company ( TSM ), which manufactures Nvidia chips, and equipment maker ASML ( ASML ) fell roughly 2% each while chip designer Arm Holdings ( ARM ) was down 4%.

Shares of memory chipmaker Micron Technology ( MU ) and peer SK Hynix ( SKHY ) also dropped more than 4%, giving back some of Monday's double-digit percentage gains. Storage and memory players SanDisk ( SNDK ), Seagate (STX ), and Western Digital ( WDC ) all fell at least 5%.

Other areas of the AI trade retreated, including neocloud providers' stocks CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius .

articles.title: Anthropic stock drops below $83 IPO price as day-one pop vanishes
articles.summary: Anthropic broke its IPO price faster than all but two of the biggest IPOs since 2008.
articles.body:
Anthropic's first trade was worth $12 billion. Three sessions later, anyone who bought it was down more than 25%.

Anthropic ( ANT ) slipped below its $83 IPO price Tuesday in its fourth session as a public company. The stock opened at $111.50 on Nov. 19 and closed its first day at $97.17 . On Friday, it came within a nickel of the line. Minutes after Tuesday's open, a share cost less than $80, about the price of Grand Theft Auto VI , the video game that launched the same day Anthropic did.

The sellers have plenty to work with. Insiders can sell up to 316 million shares, more than a quarter as many as the IPO sold, according to Anthropic's IPO filing .

ANT is still bid among individual investors, who bought about $100 million more Anthropic stock than they sold on both Friday and Monday, making it their second-most-bought stock, according to Vanda Research.

Passive index funds are next in line. Anthropic could join the Nasdaq-100 on a fast track as soon as Dec. 21, which would force index-tracking funds, such as the Invesco QQQ Trust ( QQQ ), to buy, according to a Themes ETFs analysis .

Among the 12 biggest US IPOs since 2008, only Uber ( UBER ) and Facebook, now Meta ( META ), broke their IPO prices sooner, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. Uber opened below its price in 2019. Facebook cracked in its second session in 2012. SpaceX ( SPCX ) held out for 22 sessions this year.

Breaking the IPO price is a bad start, not a verdict. What came next depended on how far each stock fell.

The shallow dips healed the fastest. Visa ( V ), Arm ( ARM ) and Alibaba ( BABA ) each bottomed within about three months, less than 20% below their IPO prices, and doubled those prices within two years.

The deep sell-offs took the long way around. Facebook sank more than 50% below its IPO price by September 2012, then doubled it two years later. Uber needed six years to double its IPO price, and GM nearly 15. Rivian ( RIVN ) and Coupang ( CPNG ) still haven't made it back.

About a quarter of the 2,734 US IPOs from 2001 through 2024 closed their first day below the offer price, and two-thirds of those were lower three years later, according to data from University of Florida professor Jay Ritter . Anthropic held its line longer than that group but not by much.

As Creative Planning's Charlie Bilello put it on X , "the best time for Wall Street to sell IPOs to the public has been the worst time for the public to buy."

articles.title: Google Cloud India Denies Mass Layoffs, Confirms 30 Roles Cut
articles.summary: Google Cloud India denies mass layoffs, confirms about 30 roles cut in a restructuring; company continues India expansion plans, including a $15B investment and AI hub.
articles.body: In a rare move, Google Cloud India took to X to deny speculation about large-scale layoffs, clarifying that it had eliminated around 30 roles in the country as part of an organisational restructuring.In a post on X, Google Cloud India said: “These rumours are totally inaccurate. Last week, Google Cloud made a small organisational change in India, and approximately 30 roles were eliminated as part of a reprioritisation of work.”The reaction came after an anonymous employee identifying himself as an L4-level staffer based in Bengaluru said they were alarmed by the volume of discussions on Blind, an anonymous workplace forum, about potential job cuts across Google Cloud’s India teams. The posts alleged that the cuts were unrelated to employee performance and that US-based counterparts had not been affected.Some sources told TOI that Google Cloud India has close to 1,300 employees, although TOI could not independently verify the figure.Google Cloud India reported revenue of Rs 2,065.4 crore in FY2025, up 3% year-on-year, and a net profit of Rs 226.8 crore, according to data from database firm The Company Check.Google Cloud generates revenue through consumption-based fees and subscriptions for its Google Cloud Platform and Google Workspace offerings, which include infrastructure, platform, applications and other cloud services. Its portfolio spans AI-optimised infrastructure, AI development platforms, cybersecurity and data and analytics services.The announcement comes even as the company ramps up investments in India. Last year, Google announced plans to invest approximately $15 billion in the country over five years (2026-2030).
